title: Angry at God
hookLine: the psalms, Job and Jeremiah all argue with God

cards: A man sits with his feet locked in the stocks at a gate by the house of the LORD. He's been beaten for delivering God's message. The next morning he's let out.
Later, the prophet Jeremiah turns to God: "O LORD, thou hast deceived me, and I was deceived: thou art stronger than I, and hast prevailed: I am in derision daily, every one mocketh me."
You tricked me, he says, and look where it got me. It's still there, in the scriptures of church and synagogue alike.

teach.h: HOW LONG, O LORD? FOUR TIMES.
teach.b: Back in year one, David shouted at God in the Psalms. He has company. Psalm thirteen opens, "How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?"
Four times, how long. It's someone pounding on a door, and it was kept in the book God's people sang together. Then Job.

teach.h: JOB: I WILL NOT REFRAIN MY MOUTH.
teach.b: Before God ever speaks, Job says, "I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul." He keeps that promise.
And he wants a hearing, not an exit: "Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments."
He talks as if God's seat were a courtroom he's desperate to get into. Then what Jeremiah does next. After accusing God, he says he'll stop speaking God's name.

teach.h: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES.
teach.b: And then: "But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay." Angry, and unable to walk away.
Anger at God, in these texts, can be a sign of how close the relationship still is. Some readers put it this way: you don't shout at someone you've stopped believing in.
Some Christians were taught that anger at God is a sin to be hidden.

teach.h: BRING IT TO THE ONE IT'S AIMED AT.
teach.b: These texts show another way: bring it, honestly, to the one it's aimed at. In the Psalms, that is prayer.

how: Some Christians pray the psalms of lament in services and alone, including their angry lines; some churches hold services of lament after tragedies, and pastors and spiritual directors encourage people to bring anger honestly to God in prayer.

o: a feeling only people without faith ever have
a sin that ends a person's place among God's people
honest fury kept in scripture as a kind of prayer

games.q: arguing with God — tap the pairs.
p: how long wilt thou forget me
I will not refrain my mouth
a burning fire shut up in my bones

s: angry prayers were edited out of the Bible
Jeremiah, Job and Psalm 13 all argue with God, and they're still there.
Jeremiah's angry prayer comes after he has been put in the stocks
he is beaten and put in the stocks, let out the next morning, and then says, thou hast deceived me.
after accusing God, Jeremiah walked away for good
he tried to stop, but God's word was like a burning fire shut up in his bones.

games.q: you're Jeremiah. you've been beaten and mocked for speaking God's word, and you've just told God he deceived you. what do you do next?
o: quit, and never speak God's name again.
try to stop, but find the word burning in you so you can't hold it in.
games.why: Jeremiah says he'll stop, then: his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones. angry, and unable to walk away.

practice: Let one anger come up that you haven't said out loud: an unfairness, a loss, a prayer that went nowhere, something done to you or someone you love.
If you pray, tell God plainly, in your own words or the psalm's, how long; if you don't, say it to the empty room or on paper.
If the anger ever turns toward harming yourself or someone else, call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Angry at God. The honest fury of Jeremiah, Job and the Psalms, kept in scripture as a kind of prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: he can take it. Jeremiah was furious, and stayed. Rest well.
